messages.subject: Re: Why does filtering or resampling reduce the bit depth?
messages.subject_clean: Why does filtering or resampling reduce the bit depth?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mickey,

I had a similar problem. Most of my files are 32 bit floating and I needed to downsample to 22050 without decreasing bit depth. In that case, using tuneR function downsample works well without decreasing bit depth.

Dan

El viernes, 10 de julio de 2020 a las 8:22:58 UTC-5, Michael Pardo escribió:
> Hi everyone,
>
> I am working with 32 bit floating point sound files. Every time I try to apply a frequency filter (ffilter, fir, bwfilter) or down-sample the sound file (resamp), the bit depth of the output wave object automatically becomes 16 bits instead of 32. Can anyone explain to me why this is happening and what I can do to fix it? I don't want to change the bit depth. I only want to filter the sound file and reduce the sampling rate.
>
> Thanks!
> Mickey

messages.subject: Using seewave with M1 Mac
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

Have any of you tried to run seewave or other sound analysis packages such as tuneR, soundgen, or phonTools on a Mac computer with an M1 processor? My computer unexpectedly died a few days ago and I’m thinking about buying an M1 MacBook, but I’m a little concerned that there might be issues with running these sound analysis packages on Apple silicon. Has anyone encountered any such issues?

Thanks,
Mickey Pardo

Sent from my iPhone
